evidence_caveat: Archive reports are historical and anecdotal. These fictional exercises demonstrate only mechanics already present in the synthetic runtime; they do not verify the reported root causes, frequency, vendor behavior, or archived incident outcomes.

exercises.version_context: CUCM, CUBE and Lync interoperation are mentioned; exact deployed versions are not stated in the initial report.
exercises.evidence_type: Customer-style incident report with troubleshooting suggestions; the original reporter's resolution is unconfirmed.
exercises.archive_issue_paraphrase: A reported blind transfer through a SIP trunk produced one-way audio. Replies discuss SDP direction and a conditional early-offer profile; another participant reports a separate header-manipulation fix.
exercises.runtime_scope: Demonstrates only a generic directional-media failure and recovery using the modeled carrier media-in setting. It does not reproduce blind transfer, a transfer-created leg, SDP renegotiation, CUBE/Lync, or early-offer trunk behavior.
exercises.assessment: Pass requires an observed ONE_WAY_MEDIA result with outbound=true and inbound=false, followed by a fresh voice interaction that reaches resolved with no obligations and has a MEDIA_PATHS trace reporting both directions true after inbound media is restored. A 200_OK or media trace without completed call handling is insufficient.

exercises.runtime_scope: Demonstrates only synthetic carrier fault injection and a fresh successful call after clearing that fault. Incident timelines, evidence confidence, status notices, alternate routing, and the historical provider event are not modeled.
exercises.assessment: Pass requires an observed SIGNALLING_FAILED result while the carrier is faulted, followed by a fresh voice interaction that reaches resolved with no obligations and has 200_OK and bidirectional MEDIA_PATHS traces after the carrier fault is cleared. A stale successful call or early 200_OK cannot satisfy recovery.
